heading: Menu items that open a page
body:
An item with a `route` opens a page of the app in the same window. Each item has an `id`, a `label`, the `route` and an optional `shortcut`. An item has exactly one of `route` or `action`. The `route` must be a static page of the app, without a query or a fragment, such as `/help`. A shortcut has one lowercase letter or digit and always includes `command`; it may add `control`, `option` and `shift`. On Linux and Windows, `command` and `control` are both Ctrl, `option` is Alt and `shift` is Shift; on macOS `control` stays Control. So two shortcuts that differ only by `control` become the same Ctrl shortcut there, and a shortcut that becomes a standard one (such as Ctrl+Q, or Ctrl+Y, which is Redo on Windows) is refused for that target with `TY1601`. There are at most 64 items in all menus, and ids and shortcuts must be unique. A wrong item (a bad id, label or shortcut, both `route` and `action`, or neither) stops the build with `TY1601`.

On iOS and Android the build prints a note, because a phone has no menu bar. On iPad the items join the File, View and Help menus of the iPad menu bar. On iPhone only items with a shortcut can be reached, with a hardware keyboard, where `command` is Command and `control` is Control. On Android the window gets an app bar with the app name, and the items are listed in its overflow menu; their shortcuts use Ctrl, as on Linux and Windows, and also show in the keyboard shortcuts list. Items with an `action` appear in the same places (see Menu actions).

Opening a page loads a new document. The services of the old page stop, and the new page starts with fresh services. Use a menu action when the item must keep the state of the page.
